headline: Aussie jobs shock and a tech rout keep the dollar near a 19-month high; AUD/USD sinks 0.9%
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.1% to near 103.9 after touching 103.97, its highest since April 2025, as a 2%-plus slide in US stocks after Anthropic's debut and Goolsbee's warning on inflation outweighed a weak Philly Fed survey. The Aussie led losses after a jobs shock, with sterling and the offshore yuan close behind, while the won, the rupee, the ringgit and the peso edged higher on exporter selling, inflows and steady oil.
drivers: Aussie jobs shock ends RBA hike talk

Employment fell 43,500 in October against a forecast 20,000–25,000 gain and unemployment jumped to 4.9%, a five-year high. Three-year yields fell more than 10bp as traders brought forward RBA cut bets, and AUD/USD lost about 0.9% to near 0.6651.
Risk-off and a hawkish Fed keep the dollar bid

US indices fell more than 2% as the AI trade cracked again, and Goolsbee said he sees no clear path back to 2% inflation. The Philly Fed index sank to 6.3 (20.0 expected) but prices paid jumped to 58.2, so the 2-year eased only about 3bp to 4.77% and the dollar firmed into the close.
Asia: exporters and central banks lean against the dollar

Korean chipmakers' dollar sales pushed the won to 1,330.0, Taiwan's central bank pulled the Taiwan dollar back to 32.942 after an intraday 33.04 as the Taiex fell 4.4%, and the offshore yuan slipped about 0.36% to near 6.691, its weakest since mid-October.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: the Fed is debating how fast to hike while the RBA, BoC and BoE look closer to done, so I back the dollar against the Aussie, the loonie and the pound on rallies. I keep fading it against the yen just under 160, where Tokyo is on guard and a deeper equity sell-off would add haven demand. A DXY close below 102.5, or soft US data that removes the 50bp December talk, would turn me neutral.
ideas: New sale on a bounce to 0.6700–0.6720 after the jobs shock turned the RBA toward cuts; for 0.6580, stop 0.6770.
Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as the 2-year gap stays wide and BoC odds slip; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4270.
Hold the sale filled at 160.00–160.20 as Tokyo guards 160 and stocks slide; for 157.50, stop 160.50.
review: AUD/USD hit its 0.6650 target to within a fraction of a pip (low 0.66503), about 250 pips banked, and I re-sell on bounces. EUR/USD is about 210 pips in favour, GBP/USD about 80, USD/CAD about 250, USD/JPY about 50 (high 159.97, stop safe), USD/CHF about 50 and the ringgit long about 0.025, so I hold all and trail stops. EUR/JPY ran up toward its 175.80 stop in the New York morning and I stand aside; the rupiah long and USD/INR short are slightly ahead, and the other ranges held, with USD/TWD again capped at 33.04.

eurusd.note: Little changed near 1.0969 after a spike to about 1.1013; the short is about 210 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: Two forces cancelled out. The euro briefly rallied to about 1.1013 when Nasdaq futures jumped ahead of Anthropic's debut and the dollar index slipped, then gave it all back as US stocks reversed to a loss of more than 2% and the dollar firmed into the close. The 2-year Treasury yield, still near 4.77%, keeps the rate gap with Bunds wide, and worries about 2027 European elections cap the euro.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short, keep the stop at 1.1020 just above Thursday's spike and extend the target to 1.0880: the Fed is set to outpace an ECB priced for little more. A close above 1.1020 would say the dollar's run has stalled.
eurusd.watch: Euro zone consumer confidence (Nov 20), flash PMIs (next week), Lagarde, ECB (Dec 17).

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces ECB, rally sold.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.46% to near 1.3086, below its October low; the short is about 80 pips in favour.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did most of the moving, and sterling had no defence. Investors moved into the US currency as equities slid, and Wednesday's steady 2.8% core CPI had already cut the odds of a December BoE hike to about 80%. The pound also eased back from a 20-month high against the euro, so there was no cross support.
gbpusd.outlook: I stay short, lower the target to 1.2950 and trail the stop to 1.3170, above Wednesday's breakdown: BoE hike odds are slipping while the Fed debates 50bp. A close back above 1.3170 would say the break has failed.
gbpusd.watch: UK retail sales (Nov 20), UK flash PMIs (next week), UK budget headlines, BoE (Dec 17).

view.call: Short 1.3150–1.3180; soft core CPI trims BoE hike odds.

audusd.note: Down about 0.9% to near 0.6651, a 10-month low; the sale hit its 0.6650 target to within a pip.
audusd.why: The Aussie did the moving. October jobs fell 43,500 against a forecast gain of about 20,000–25,000 and unemployment jumped to 4.9%, a five-year high, so traders dropped RBA hike bets and pulled the first cut forward to September next year; UBS now sees August. A 2% slide in US stocks and weaker metals added to the selling into the New York close.
audusd.outlook: I book the old sale and re-sell a bounce to 0.6700–0.6720 for 0.6580: the RBA has turned toward cuts while the Fed is still hiking. A close above 0.6770 would say the sell-off is exhausted.
audusd.watch: RBA speakers, China loan prime rates (Nov 20), Australia monthly CPI (Nov 25), US PCE (late Nov).

view.call: Sell 0.6700–0.6720; jobs shock turns RBA toward cuts.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.17% to near 159.60 after getting within 3 pips of 160; my sale is about 50 pips in favour.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Safe-haven buying faded early as Nasdaq futures rallied on Anthropic's IPO, and Ueda said financial conditions remain easy, which traders read as no hurry beyond a December hike, so the pair pressed 160 (high 159.97). Tokyo's line held, and the late stock slide and a 3bp drop in the 2-year yield kept the dollar from breaking through.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 157.50 with the stop at 160.50: Tokyo has capped 160 all month, a December BoJ hike is the consensus, and a deeper equity sell-off favours the yen. A close above 160.50 would show Tokyo is standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments near 160, BoJ speakers, Japan's monthly intervention data (Nov 30).

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; Tokyo guards 160, stocks sliding.

usdchf.note: Up slightly to near 0.8439, holding at an 18-month high; my long is about 50 pips in favour.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving, gently. Even with US stocks down more than 2%, the franc drew little haven demand because the SNB's 0% rate makes it a funding currency while the Fed debates bigger hikes. Goolsbee's warning that inflation is well above target kept the rate gap wide.
usdchf.outlook: I hold the long for 0.8500 and raise the stop to 0.8400: the rate gap keeps widening and the franc is not acting as a haven. A close below 0.8400 would say the breakout has failed.
usdchf.watch: Fed speakers, SNB comments, Swiss CPI (early Dec), Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: Long 0.8380–0.8400; rate gap, franc funds carry.

usdcad.note: Up slightly to near 1.4339 after a new 19-month high around 1.4358; the buy is about 250 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: The rate gap did the moving. Scotiabank points to the widening spread between US and Canadian short-term rates as the main driver, with the BoC at 2.50% against a Fed range of 3.75–4.00% that may rise in December. Risk aversion lifted the dollar further, and a 0.7% rise in crude and a report that Canada is seeking an interim US tariff deal did little for the loonie.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for 1.4450 and raise the stop to 1.4270: the policy gap is the widest of this cycle and swaps now give a December BoC hike only about 67%. A sharp oil rebound or a tariff deal would be the main threats.
usdcad.watch: Canada retail sales (Nov 20), US-Canada tariff talks, oil and Hormuz headlines, Canada Q3 GDP (late Nov).

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; rate gap widest of the cycle.

usdcnh.note: Offshore yuan fell about 0.36% to near 6.691 after touching about 6.70, its weakest since mid-October.
usdcnh.why: The yuan did the moving, late. The Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen ended without a clear trade breakthrough, and as US stocks slid the offshore yuan lost about 0.5% at worst in thin trading. Bank of America said the long yuan rally had left traders unprepared for a pullback, while onshore turnover stayed light, which suggests stop-losses rather than a policy change.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: exporters tend to sell dollars when onshore trading resumes and the PBOC has been fixing the yuan stronger. A close above 6.70 would open 6.75 and show Beijing is letting it slip.
usdcnh.watch: PBOC fixing vs estimates and loan prime rates (Nov 20), US-China follow-up talks, China data (late Nov).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC fixings and exporters vs dollar strength.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.8447, about 50 pips from the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved it. The wide gap between US rates and HIBOR keeps the carry trade into US dollars attractive and holds the Hong Kong dollar near the weak side of its band, while the HKMA's commitment at 7.85 caps the pair. Hong Kong stocks tracked the regional tech sell-off without changing the picture.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: carry keeps it near 7.85, and only a HIBOR jump or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.16% to near 1.2914, at the top of my 1.2780–1.2920 range.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. The broad risk-off move, a 4.4% plunge in Taiwan stocks and a weaker yuan pulled regional currencies lower, and the Singapore dollar followed. The MAS policy band, which keeps the currency strong against its trade-weighted basket, limited the damage.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range for now: the MAS band anchors the Singapore dollar while a hiking Fed keeps the pair firm. A close above 1.2920 would open 1.3000.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore final Q3 GDP and CPI (late Nov), yuan fixings, Fed speakers, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won rose 3.0 to 1,330.0 in Seoul, a fourth daily gain, after touching 1,327.0.
usdkrw.why: Exporters did the moving. Chipmakers sold dollars from booming semiconductor sales as Korea's exports for the year passed $1 trillion, and a drop in oil helped, while the Kospi rose 1.4% to 5,137.89. Importer buying near 1,320 and foreign net selling of Korean shares limited the gain as the dollar index hit 103.97.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling caps the pair, but foreign stock selling and a hawkish Fed limit won gains, and the US tech rout points to more outflows. A Seoul close below 1,325 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows after the US tech rout, Fed speakers, oil, Korea November exports (Dec 1).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar edged up 0.5 cents to 32.942 after an intraday 33.04, as the Taiex fell 4.4%.
usdtwd.why: The central bank did the moving at the close. Foreigners sold another NT$24.3bn of Taiwan shares, a fourth straight day and over NT$200bn in total, as the Taiex plunged 1,768 points, and the pair traded above 33 for much of the day. Exporters sold dollars near 33 and local dealers said the central bank stepped in during the final minutes to turn a loss into a small gain.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are clearly defending 33, but heavy outflows keep pressure on, and Taiwan's new short-selling curbs from Nov 20 may slow the stock slide. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, central bank action near 33, Taiwan export orders (Nov 20), central bank meeting (mid-Dec).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit firmed to 4.1100/1145 at the 6pm KL close from 4.1130/1180; my long is about 0.025 ahead.
usdmyr.why: Malaysia did the moving, a little. Third-quarter GDP growth beat the advance estimate, lifting growth for the first nine months to 5.6%, and Bank Muamalat said bargain hunters stepped in because a 50bp Fed hike is far from certain. The dollar index's dip during Asian hours helped.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the long for 4.150 with the stop at 4.090: Fed hike bets and regional equity outflows outweigh a steady Bank Negara. A close below 4.090 would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia October CPI (late Nov), oil and palm oil, regional chip stocks, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; Fed hike bets outweigh a steady BNM.

usdphp.note: Peso gained 4.5 centavos to 63.665 at the BAP close, mid-way in my range.
usdphp.why: Oil did the moving. RCBC's Ricafort pointed to slightly lower crude, which led to sharp cuts in local pump prices and should trim the oil import bill and the current account deficit. The move was small as the dollar stayed near its 19-month high.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: cheaper oil, holiday remittances and a possibly hawkish BSP help, but the Fed weighs. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: Oil and Hormuz headlines, BSP comments, Fed speakers, BSP decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; oil, remittances and BSP vs Fed.

usdidr.note: Rupiah slipped about 0.1% to near 18,235 a day after BI's hike; JISDOR 18,269. Long slightly ahead.
usdidr.why: The dollar did the moving, and the hike did not stick. Bank Indonesia's surprise 25bp rise to 6.00% lifted the rupiah only 0.1% on Wednesday, and it gave that back as the dollar held near a 19-month high and other Asian currencies firmed without it. Political worries and foreign outflows ahead of MSCI changes keep demand for dollars high.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long for 18,500 with the stop at 18,150: even a surprise hike has not turned the rupiah, and outflows persist. A close below 18,150 would show BI has turned the tide.
usdidr.watch: BI intervention, MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; hike failed to lift rupiah, outflows persist.

usdinr.note: Rupee rose for a fourth day to about 93.30–93.36, after trading 93.17–93.55.
usdinr.why: Foreign inflows did the moving. Foreign investors bought Indian shares and returned to government bonds, and the rupee reversed morning losses as local stocks rallied, making it Asia's best performer this month. ICICI Securities said it has broken out of its 94.15–96.85 range, though a rebound in crude capped the gain.
usdinr.outlook: I hold the short, extend the target to 92.80 below 93.00 support and trim the stop to 93.60: inflows are doing the work. RBI dollar buying to rebuild reserves is the main risk; a close above 93.60 would end the call.
usdinr.watch: Foreign equity and bond flows, oil, India flash PMIs (next week), RBI decision (Dec 4).

view.call: Short from 93.50–93.60; FPI inflows, range breakout.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.1% to near 175.07 after a New York morning run toward 175.8; I stand aside.
eurjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Early in New York the euro rallied and USD/JPY pressed 160 at the same time, so the cross rose about 0.3% toward my 175.80 stop as haven demand for the yen faded on Anthropic's debut. It eased back as stocks reversed, but the call no longer has a clean edge.
eurjpy.outlook: I treat the sale as stopped and hold a 174.0–176.5 range: the euro is weak, but the yen is not gaining while USD/JPY sits near 160. A close below 174.0 would revive the short.
eurjpy.watch: Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments near 160, euro zone flash PMIs (next week).

view.call: 174.0–176.5; weak euro, yen stuck near Tokyo's line.

cnhjpy.note: Down about 0.2% to near 23.85, mid-way in my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: The yuan did the moving. The offshore yuan fell about 0.36% in thin late trading after the Shenzhen summit brought no clear trade deal, while the yen weakened less against the dollar, so the cross slipped. Both currencies remain managed: Beijing slows the yuan, Tokyo guards 160.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close below 23.6 would show the yuan's pullback is spreading.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings and loan prime rates (Nov 20), Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments.

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

eurcnh.note: Up about 0.3% to near 7.340, mid-range in my 7.28–7.40 band.
eurcnh.why: The yuan did the moving. The euro was flat against the dollar, while the offshore yuan fell about 0.36% to its weakest since mid-October after the APEC summit ended without a trade breakthrough, so the cross rose.
eurcnh.outlook: I keep a 7.28–7.40 range: euro weakness should resume, while the PBOC leans against a faster yuan slide. A close above 7.40 would open 7.45.
eurcnh.watch: PBOC fixings (daily), euro zone flash PMIs (next week), ECB (Dec 17).

view.call: 7.28–7.40; weak euro vs PBOC brake on yuan.

watch: Next: Japan CPI, China's loan prime rates, Taiwan export orders and UK and Canada retail sales (Nov 20), flash PMIs next week, Australia CPI (Nov 25) and US PCE (late Nov), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and ECB, BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
